findings.claim: The NETFRAMEWORK guard suppresses ExcludeFromCodeCoverage on every .NET Framework target, including .NET Framework 4.x where ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is available. Consequently, generated formatters and resolvers compiled for a supported target such as net472 are not decorated, contrary to the requirement that all generated code be decorated except where conditional emission is needed for compilation.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.NetFrameworkGeneratedCodeCoverageAttributeTests.NetFrameworkGeneratedCodeIncludesAvailableAttribute. It generates a formatter and resolver against the net472 reference assemblies with NETFRAMEWORK and NET472 defined and asserts that every generated source contains the attribute. It fails on head because the NETFRAMEWORK branch removes it, even though the attribute exists in .NET Framework 4.7.2. The same guard appears in all the changed templates.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Decoration is always on for every emitted formatter, resolver, and nested helper/cache class, with preprocessor guards only to keep target frameworks compiling; no generator option is added. This is the broad scope implemented by the change.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Only formatter types, including object, string-key, enum, and union formatters, need decoration. Resolvers and nested helper/cache classes are outside the requested scope, so the resolver and composite-resolver template additions would be removed while retaining the formatter additions.
